What are your favorite tips and tricks for saving money at home? How do you squeeze every penny out of a dollar? When do you splurge to have a luxury or buy the good stuff?
Watch your pennies and your dollars will watch themselves.

Avoid buy one get one half off and 10 for 10 deals, etc.

These types of sales are a psychological trick. If you intend to spend two dollars on two items you aren't a getting a deal buying 10. You've just overspent and bought more than you needed.

Also understand that stores are designed to make you impulse buy and many chain stores are specifically designed to exploit a woman's psychology. Always keep it clear in your head what are wants and what are needs.

Make a budget for play time just as you do for serious stuff.

Budget is a priority, we've been talking about starting to spend like we were living on one income to build up our savings and practice for when I eventually leave my job. I'm a sucker for a bargain, its a character flaw and I'm aware of it so I can actively mitigate against it.

Transitioning into one income habits before you need to is smart. Your bargain monster can be a hard beast to tame. Remember those dishelved racks are meant to exploit a woman's gathering instinct.

I always budget around the minimum income instead of maximum. I picked this habit up in business and it transitions well into home finance.

On bargain shopping: Know what price to set out to beat. It cuts down on frivolous spending and bad deals. I use Aldi/Costco frequently for that baseline to compare.

A big deal is that I devote a lot of house space to storage of these things. Last year I used aldi flour that I got for $.99 at their November/December sale until late summer before having to buy more at $1.29/$1.49 regular price. So this year I bought more. I bake all our bread, pizza doughs ect. so this is a huge savings for us.

Another example, Aldi detergent is $1.89 for '32 loads' (you can use half that). That comes out to 6 cents a load, cheaper than making it yourself, which I looked into. So I don't buy other sales unless it's better than that.

Do you have a favorite bread recipe, blog, or cookbook? I grab my laundry detergent at Costco, I don't have an aldi but shop at my local grocery outlet store, their products change often as its usually overstock or misprinted items. I also buy from a bulk store for most of my dry goods. We have a great local market here in town.

Sounds like you have some nice resources! I'm flattered by your interest!

I use Joy of cooking and the Internet for recipes. "Joy" is a reprint that has WWII recipes and some new ones. Love the index.

I should make a post with my bread recipe, I typed it up for a friend, but I'm on mobile. It's basically 3cups flour, sprinkle of yeast and a cup of water. It's very forgiving, but can change a lot based on timing.

I like to buy fewer of quality stuff than many cheap things. Better to buy a $50 toaster that lasts 10 years than buy a $20 toaster every couple of years.

Second-hand stores are good for getting quality things for a good price (excluding time). You might even find a $5 toaster that doesn't break in 15 years but is repairable.

You can't beat a thrift store for most clothing, toys, furniture, and appliance needs. I like to check out my local auction sometimes too, we have one in town every Friday night, they auction off boxes of stuff for as little as $3.
